name: Walk-Behind Floor Sweeper
definition: A commercial sweeper whose operator walks behind and steers the machine during normal sweeping, with manual propulsion or powered traction and model-specific brush, hopper and dust-control systems.
includedScope: Battery or engine powered walk-behind vacuum sweepers
excludedScope: Hazardous or combustible-dust work without explicit approval
headline: Walk-behind floor sweeper types, dust control, hopper systems and buyer checks
description: This profile separates manual and powered walk-behind sweepers and explains brush paths, hopper handling, dust control, route fit and model-specific procurement evidence.
metaDescription: Walk-behind floor sweeper technical guide covering manual and powered types, dust filters, hoppers, specifications, models and buyer checks.
disclaimer: This independent category reference is not model-specific purchasing, safety, hazardous-material, textile-care or repair advice. Confirm the current manual, exact configuration, serial range, local compliance and service terms before procurement or use.

keyFacts.label: Category boundary
keyFacts.value: Operator walks behind during normal sweeping
keyFacts.evidence: Reviewed official ranges explicitly classify manual and powered machines as walk-behind sweepers.
keyFacts.scope: Named commercial models; no universal width threshold.

keyFacts.label: Propulsion
keyFacts.evidence: Official sources distinguish manual, battery and powered walk-behind formats.

keyFacts.label: Dust control
keyFacts.value: Passive collection or active vacuum and filtration
keyFacts.evidence: Powered vacuum sweeper sources publish filter systems; manual products may omit active suction.

keyFacts.label: Buyer verification
keyFacts.value: Measure complete width, turning, operator force, hopper handling and dust exposure
keyFacts.evidence: Official specifications use model- and configuration-specific reporting boundaries.
keyFacts.scope: Quoted regional configuration and actual buyer site.

systemFlow.name: Edge gathering
systemFlow.role: Moves edge debris toward the main path.
systemFlow.evidence: Official product sources identify one or two side brushes.

systemFlow.name: Main sweeping
systemFlow.role: Transfers loose debris toward the hopper.
systemFlow.evidence: Manufacturer sources identify cylindrical or tandem brush systems.

systemFlow.name: Collection
systemFlow.evidence: Official specifications publish hopper volume and handling features.
systemFlow.scope: Volume is not a mass rating.

systemFlow.name: Dust management
systemFlow.role: Reduces airborne dust on equipped machines.
systemFlow.evidence: Powered-model sources describe filtration and filter cleaning.

variants.name: Manual push
variants.taskScale: Small areas and rapid spot routes
variants.limitations: Operator effort and dust control differ from powered vacuum sweepers.

variants.name: Battery walk-behind
variants.operatorRelationship: Operator walks behind powered traction or brush drive
variants.limitations: Runtime and productivity depend on configuration and route.
variants.evidence: Nilfisk, Kärcher and Wetrok list battery walk-behind machines.

variants.name: Industrial powered walk-behind
variants.operatorRelationship: Powered drive with manual steering and dumping
variants.spaceConstraints: Larger aisle-turn and hopper handling space
variants.limitations: Dust and debris approval remains model-specific.
variants.evidence: Tennant identifies S10 as an industrial walk-behind sweeper.

performanceMetrics.name: Hopper volume

applicationFit.wcbAssessment: A full-route trial should include tight turns, representative debris and hopper emptying.

applicationFit.limitations: No achieved site output is established.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Time a complete route and inspect residual dust.
applicationFit.evidence: Manufacturers position reviewed machines for warehouses and industry.
applicationFit.assessment: A full-route trial should include tight turns, representative debris and hopper emptying.

applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Noise, operator force, dust release and pedestrian separation matter more than maximum width.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Trial the machine during representative traffic conditions.
applicationFit.evidence: TASKI and Kärcher position compact sweepers for indoor and outdoor commercial areas.
applicationFit.assessment: Noise, operator force, dust release and pedestrian separation matter more than maximum width.

applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Surface joints, gradients, wind and wet debris require demonstration.
applicationFit.limitations: Road use and wet pickup are outside scope.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Test ramps and rough sections and confirm storage conditions.
applicationFit.evidence: Reviewed sources include indoor and outdoor use for selected models.
applicationFit.assessment: Surface joints, gradients, wind and wet debris require demonstration.

procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Treating theoretical m²/h as delivered output
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Include travel, turns, dumping and filter care.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Record debris load and remaining dust.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Manufacturers publish nominal or theoretical outputs.

procurementDecisions.assessment: Inspect media, seals, airflow and cleaning together.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Obtain written approval for the dust and trial the machine.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Verify filter and seal part numbers.

procurementDecisions.assessment: Measure the entire route and emptying task.
procurementDecisions.basis: Machine and turning envelopes exceed brush width.
procurementDecisions.limitations: Published data cannot represent every obstruction.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Demonstrate doors, turns, ramps and storage.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Measure operator push, lift and dump demands.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official sources publish dimensions and hopper arrangements.

engineeringChecks.reason: Wet, hot, toxic or combustible material may be prohibited.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Document material and obtain written manufacturer approval.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Manufacturer documentation limits intended material and use.

engineeringChecks.reason: Brush width does not equal machine or turning width.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Measure doors, aisles, ramps, lifts and storage.

engineeringChecks.reason: Wear parts and electrical systems are model-specific.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Record model, serial range and exact service part numbers.

standards.name: IEC 60335-2-72:2021
standards.applicability: Particular safety requirements for powered commercial floor-treatment machines, including sweepers; it is not a cleaning-performance ranking.
standards.evidence: IEC publishes edition 5.0 and its commercial floor-treatment scope.
standards.scope: Confirm regional adoption and exact machine classification.

developments.title: IEC commercial floor-treatment safety edition published
developments.evidence: The IEC catalogue records the edition and publication date.
developments.scope: Safety scope only; not a category-wide performance claim.
